title: scoring_status computes pending but reports in_progress as literal 0, so pending applications vanish from the totals
detail: The seeded a-ciara analysis is Pending, so pending=1 for its vacancy, but the returned tuple is (in_progress=0, completed=total-pending, failed=0). in_progress+completed+failed != total; the scoring status UI will show one application unaccounted for.
recommended_fix: Return #(pending, total - pending, 0, total, False) so the pending application is counted as in progress.

title: vacancy_detail hardcodes remindable_count: 2 and followup_count: 1 for every vacancy, contradicting the seeded awaiting list
detail: awaiting_count is derived per vacancy, but remindable/followup counts are constants. Non-maples vacancies have an empty awaiting list yet claim 2 remindable; for v-maples only emma.doyle has reminded: False (the other two are True), so 2 contradicts the seed data too.
recommended_fix: Derive remindable_count and followup_count from the same awaiting() data (reminded == False and followup_due == True) per vacancy.

title: UserConfirmedApproval refetches the leaderboard post-mutation with a justification comment; UserConfirmedRejection and UserConfirmedBackwardTransition do the identical mutation without the refetch
detail: The comment documents a staleness problem that applies equally to rejection and backward transitions, yet only the approval arm carries the refetch. Either the refetch is needed (then all three arms need it) or it is redundant (then drop it).
recommended_fix: Apply the same post-mutation leaderboard refetch in UserConfirmedRejection and UserConfirmedBackwardTransition, or explain why approval alone needs it.

title: Vacancy/status mutations return Ok unconditionally — the Result error channel is dead and nonexistent ids report success
detail: change_status, archive_vacancy, restore_vacancy and close_vacancy all return Ok even when no vacancy/application id matched (list.map changes nothing). demo_api.respond_result handles an Error that can never occur; failures are silently reported as success.
recommended_fix: Check find_vacancy/find_application after the map and return Error(Nil) when nothing matched, or change the return type to a plain value and drop respond_result.

title: mark_opened doc claims an idempotent Submitted→UnderReview transition but the implementation applies it unconditionally to any status
detail: change_status performs no check on the application's current status, so mark_opened on an Approved or Rejected application silently moves it to UnderReview and appends an audit entry. The documented precondition is not enforced.
recommended_fix: In mark_opened (or a dedicated change_status wrapper), only transition when the current status is Submitted; otherwise leave the store unchanged.

title: create_vacancy derives the vacancy id from an 8-char-truncated property-name slug with no uniqueness check — duplicate ids collide
detail: Two vacancies whose names share the first 8 slug chars (e.g. 'Maples Court A' / 'Maples Court B') both get id v-demo-maples-c and short_code RTDEMOmaples-c. find_vacancy then resolves every lookup and mutation to the first one; the second is unreachable.
recommended_fix: Append a disambiguator (sequence number or count of existing demo vacancies) to the suffix, or check for an existing id and extend it until unique.

title: send_bulk_invite ignores the typed emails and returns a canned invalid_emails address the landlord never entered
evidence:
#(
    store,
    BulkInviteResult(
      sent: 2,
      invalid: 1,
      invalid_emails: ["bad@example.ie"],
      trimmed: 0,
    ),
  )
detail: demo_api.send_bulk_invite takes _emails and the store returns a fixed result. Whatever the landlord types, the UI will report 2 sent and name bad@example.ie as invalid — a visibly wrong response to valid input in a sales demo.
recommended_fix: Parse the submitted emails (split on newlines/commas, validate) and compute sent/invalid/invalid_emails from the actual input.

title: send_reminder/remind_applicant thread a 'next' store that is always the unchanged input store; demo_api discards it
location: client/src/demo/demo_store.gleam:pub fn send_reminder + client/src/demo/demo_api.gleam:pub fn send_reminder
detail: The tuple shape implies a mutation that never happens (store returned unchanged, then discarded). Consequently the awaiting list's reminded flags never flip after a 'successful' reminder, so the demo UI state does not reflect the action.
recommended_fix: Either mutate the awaiting rows (set reminded: True) and thread the store through, or drop the tuple and return the count pair directly.

title: Doc comment describing id_suffix is attached to add_days_iso; id_suffix itself is undocumented
detail: The first two doc lines describe id_suffix (defined at the bottom of the file with no doc comment) but are merged into add_days_iso's documentation. Misplaced docs mislead readers and generated docs.
recommended_fix: Move the id_suffix sentences into a /// block directly above fn id_suffix, leaving only the add_days_iso description here.

title: status_from_slug silently coerces any unknown status slug to Submitted
detail: set_status accepts an arbitrary slug from the message; a typo or unexpected value becomes Submitted in state while the audit entry records the raw slug — state and audit trail disagree, and no error surfaces.
recommended_fix: Return Result(ApplicationStatus, Nil) from status_from_slug and have change_status produce Error on an unrecognised slug.

title: fetch_leaderboard_page discards the page argument and always serves the full leaderboard
detail: UserClickedLoadMoreApplications increments leaderboard_page and dispatches ApiReturnedLeaderboardPage, but the mock returns the complete list every time. If the shared response arm appends page results (the reason pagination exists), repeat clicks duplicate rows; the page parameter is dead.
recommended_fix: Slice the derived entries by page size and requested page, or cap the demo so Load More can never appear and remove the handler.
